title: Area of a parallelogram and trapezium
summary: Calculate areas and recover missing dimensions using perpendicular height.
objectives: Calculate the area of a parallelogram from its base and perpendicular height.
Calculate the area of a trapezium from its parallel sides and perpendicular height.
Rearrange area formulae to find an unknown dimension.

blocks.text: Calculate areas and recover missing dimensions using perpendicular height. Keep every measurement in compatible units before substituting.

A parallelogram has area base×perpendicular height. The height must meet the base at 90°, even when it falls outside the sloping side. A trapezium has area one half times the sum of its parallel sides times the perpendicular height.

Choose either parallel side as the parallelogram base, then pair it with the corresponding perpendicular height. For a trapezium, identify the parallel pair before substituting. Keep units consistent and square the final length unit because area measures two-dimensional coverage.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: A trapezium has parallel sides 8 cm and 14 cm and height 6 cm. Find its area.

sections.verification_note: The result uses compatible units and agrees with the dimensions and component structure.

prompt.text: A trapezium has area 126 cm², height 9 cm and one parallel side 10 cm. Find the other parallel side.

blocks.text: Do not use a sloping side as the height. Do not forget to add the parallel sides before halving. State cm² or m² for an area and check that a recovered length is positive and plausible.

prompt.text: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find its area in cm².

blocks.text: Sketch or decompose the figure, label compatible units, select the correct area or volume relationship, calculate in clear stages, and check that the final unit is squared or cubed as required.
